html:
In the summer of 1971 smallpox broke out in Aralsk, a fishing port on the Aral Sea in Kazakhstan. Ten people fell ill and three died, among them two children. The Soviet Union kept it secret, and the outside world learned of it only in 2002.

The likely source was Vozrozhdeniya Island in the Aral Sea, where the Soviet army tested biological weapons. A research ship sailed near the island while a smallpox weapon was being tested, and a young scientist on board fell ill and carried the disease home. Health officials stopped the outbreak with quarantine and the mass vaccination of some 50,000 people.

It is one of the few known escapes of a disease prepared as a weapon. It happened as the world was close to ending smallpox; the last natural case came in 1977. The Soviet germ weapons programme went on in secret despite the treaty of 1972 that banned such weapons. As the Aral Sea shrank, the island joined the mainland, raising fears about buried anthrax, which was cleaned up in 2002.
